tasks.q: What is the largest number that 8 bits can store?
tasks.fb: All eight place values added together: 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 255.

tasks.q: Which bit is the most significant bit?
a: The leftmost bit, with the place value 128
The rightmost bit, with place value 1
tasks.fb: Most significant means it makes the biggest difference to the value.

tasks.q: Changing the least significant bit from 0 to 1 changes the number by how much?
tasks.fb: The LSB is the ones column.

tasks.q: Add these two binary numbers. Tick the overflow box only if the answer needs a 9th bit.

tasks.fb: Binary has no digit 2, so it carries into the next column.

tasks.q: Add these two binary numbers, and tick the overflow box if the answer needs a 9th bit.
tasks.fb: 240 + 20 = 260, which is more than 255, so there is an overflow.

a: The result of a calculation is too large for the number of bits available
A number that is too small to store
A file that is too big for the disk
A program that runs too long

tasks.q: How can a programmer avoid overflow errors?
a: Use a data type with enough bits for the largest possible value
tasks.fb: 16 or 32 bits gives much more headroom.

tasks.q: How many values can 16 bits represent?
Add these two binary numbers, and tick the overflow box if needed.
tasks.fb: 198 + 87 = 285, which needs a 9th bit, so there is an overflow error.

info.title: Counting on fingers
info.text: In binary you can count to 31 on one hand: each finger is a place value, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16.

info.title: Ariane 5
info.text: In 1996 a rocket was destroyed 40 seconds after launch because a number too large was squeezed into too few bits.

info.title: Gandhi's nukes
info.text: A famous game bug turned a peaceful leader aggressive when a value dropped below zero and wrapped around, though the story is partly myth.

info.title: Two's complement
info.text: Negative numbers are stored using two's complement, where the MSB signals the sign. That's A level, but it starts here.

info.title: Why 255 appears everywhere
info.text: Colour values often run 0 to 255 because each colour channel is stored in one byte.

info.title: Odd or even
info.text: The least significant bit tells you instantly whether a binary number is odd (1) or even (0).
